merger_description:
Insurance Building Australia Operations Pty Ltd (the **Acquirer**), the operating entity for Ambrose Construct Group, proposes to acquire 100% of the issued shares in Major LB Pty Ltd, the operating entity for Major Loss Builders (the **Target**).

Ambrose Construct Group (**ACG**) is a national insurance repair and restoration company with a focus on services provided under insurance claims, servicing contracts directly with insurers and indirectly with insurance loss adjusters. ACG is comprised of the Ambrose Construct, Construct Services, Xtreme Clean, FEN Australia, Nexus Project Group and Abril Building Solutions and Restorations brands. ACG is majority owned by funds managed or advised by CPE Capital, an Australian private capital manager.

Major Loss Builders (**MLB**) is an insurance building specialist supplying large loss commercial and residential insurance building services in Western Australia, South Australia and the Northern Territory.

Both ACG and MLB overlap in the supply of insurance repair and restoration services for insurance claims, including business-as-usual repairs, emergency ‘make-safe’ services and associated services.

determination_table_content.details:
Insurance Building Australia Operations Pty Ltd, the operating entity
of Ambrose Construct Group, proposes to acquire all of the issued
shares in Major LB Pty Ltd, which is the operating entity of Major
Loss Builders (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The Acquirer, Insurance Building Australia Operations Pty Ltd, is the
operating entity for Ambrose Construct Group (ACG). ACG is a
national insurance repair and restoration company with a focus on
services provided under national insurance claims. It services
contracts with insurers and with insurance loss adjusters, which are
hired by insurers to investigate damage and loss on insurance
claims. ACG is majority owned by funds managed or advised by CPE
Capital, which is an Australian private capital manager.
The Target, Major LB Pty Ltd, is the operating entity of Major Loss
Builders (MLB). MLB is an insurance building specialist which
supplies complex, large loss commercial and residential insurance
building repairs in Western Australia, South Australia and the
Northern Territory.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
ACG and MLB together (the Parties) overlap in the supply of
insurance repair and restoration services for insured property
pursuant to insurance claims, including business-as-usual repairs as
well as emergency ‘mark-safe’ services, and associated services.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information submitted by third parties and
information from prior ACCC informal merger assessments. A third
party raised concerns that the Acquisition would increase
consolidation in the relevant market and make it difficult for
independent suppliers with less scale to compete.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• the Parties’ national and state-based market share aggregations
are estimated to be minimal.
• the Parties would likely continue to be constrained by a large
number of alternative suppliers of insurance restoration and
repair services nationally and alternatively in State-based based
markets in Western Australia, South Australia and the Northern
Territory.
• barriers to entry and expansion appear low to moderate. New
entrants are required to obtain panel appointments from
insurance customers, which are often influenced by existing
relationships and demonstrated experience, alongside price and
service quality levels. Independent suppliers with less scale may
face challenges competing to service insurance customers,
however the Acquisition would not meaningfully raise these
barriers.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
